summary: Reproduced the MiniMax sparse-prefill score-buffer width defect in the checked-out implementation on one gfx950 GPU. With live seq_lens=[64,4096], changing only max_seqlen_k from 4096 to stale 64 corrupted top-k output in the long sequence. The fix enlarges the score allocation only when the live sequence lengths require more block columns and emits a warning. The regression fails on the unguarded base, passes with the fix, checks exact and same-block boundaries, and validates the correctly sized GPU result against an independent Torch reference.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual unmodified Triton kernel on gfx950: correct-width and stale-width calls had identical shapes (1,65,16), but 34/1040 top-k entries differed, with 0 mismatches in the short sequence and all 34 in the long sequence. Raw log: raw/repro-before.log.

Failing-before regression: the correctly sized call matched the independent Torch reference, while the stale call differed in 116/1040 entries on this allocator layout. Raw log: raw/regression-before.log.

3 GPU tests passed: stale 64 versus live 4096 became bit-exact to the correct-width call; correct-width output matched an independent CPU Torch block-score/top-k reference; exact 4096 and same-block 4095 boundaries did not enlarge or warn. Raw log: raw/regression-final-registered.log.
All applicable repository file checks passed, including AST, isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell, and registered-test CI validation. Raw log: raw/precommit-final.log.

Neighboring legacy FP8 test could not collect because it imports the removed pre-refactor sglang.srt.layers.attention.minimax_sparse_ops.decode module. No GPU assertion ran. Raw log: raw/neighboring-fp8-collection.log.

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), unique ID 0x593d46f1dbb5dce5, executed the actual prefill and top-k Triton kernels. Device evidence: raw/gpu-info.log; numerical evidence: raw/repro-before.log and raw/regression-final-registered.log.

remaining_limitations: No GB200/SM100 was available, so the reported CUDA Xid 31 and compute-sanitizer trace were not reproduced.
No MiniMax-M3 model weights or production serving topology were used; model semantic accuracy, overlap-scheduler timing, TP=4, NCCL watchdog behavior, and multi-node behavior remain unverified.
The deterministic fixture validates the vulnerable score-buffer and top-k kernel path only.
The underlying producer of stale max_seqlen_k metadata remains unchanged; this patch hardens the allocation boundary and logs divergence.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The neighboring legacy FP8 test is currently blocked at collection by a stale module import unrelated to this patch.
